newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ANZ union sets NSW stop work meetings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ANZ union sets NSW stop work meetings.

text.p: The Finance Sector Union (FSU) said on Wednesday it had called a stop work meeting on Friday for all Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) members working in the state of New South Wales (NSW).
The meetings, to be held at several venues in the state, would consider strike action in an escalation of a dispute over job losses, the union said in a statement.

At nationwide stop work meetings last week, ANZ's FSU members voted to give the bank until 0600 GMT (05.00 p.m.) today to respond to demands regarding voluntary redundancies, job losses, retraining and redeployment.
ANZ spokesman David Wilson told Reuters the bank had already spoken with the union.
"We have made certain indications to the FSU which are in response to issues that they have raised with us ... We're still hopeful we can have meaningful discussion with the FSU," he said.
Wilson declined to elaborate on what precise indications were made.
Last month, the FSU said an ongoing efficiency drive at ANZ might see job losses of up to 5,000 over the next six months.

"We've always steered away from that figure because it is not one that the bank has endorsed. We have made it clear we are not talking about a number of staff that we intend to shed," ANZ's Wilson said.
He said the bank's position on staff numbers would be made known "in the next few months."
Wilson said the FSU had made no direct threat of strike action to ANZ.
ANZ shares closed five cents lower at A$7.38.
